name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite, and the binding constraint is financing, not saturation. Datacenter and robot ceilings are lifted an order of magnitude (60,000 TWh / 3,000 per 1000 workers) so they never bind within the horizon; automation gains a production payoff (robots ~2 worker-equivalents each per Acemoglu-Restrepo 2020 magnitudes; compute ~100k worker-equivalents/TWh, i.e. today's ~500 TWh augments ~1% of the workforce); and the energy-capex share of investment is endogenous (competes for the savings pool up to 60%, vs the baseline's fixed 30% ramp). What limits growth here is savings, WACC, and regional financing spreads — the model's financing machinery — rather than assumed demand ceilings. The baseline retains all ceilings and zero payoff; this scenario is the explicit alternative hypothesis, not a calibrated forecast.
